Author: Surepalli Nanda Bench: Surepalli Nanda  HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE SUREPALLI NANDA  WRIT PETITION No.17532 OF 2023 ORDER:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondents.
2. The petitioners approached the Court seeking the prayer as follows:
"To issue an order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the 2nd and 3rd respondents in not considering pending application dated 05.01.2023 and 02.02.2023 submitted by the petitioners to refer the award No.12/2019 dated 24.07.2019 and Award No.13/2019 dated 30.07.2019 to the authority for enhancement of the compensation in respect of the land in Sy.No.265 admeasuring Ac.41-12 guntas situated at Pothireddypally village,
Thimmajipet Mandal, Nagarkurnool District, though the petitioners received the awarded compensation under the protest, as illegal unlawful contrary to law and consequently direct the 2nd and 3rd respondents to refer the above two awards for enhancement of the compensation to the authority under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act 2013 and pass such other order or orders which are necessary in the interest of justice."
WP_17532_2023 SN,J 3. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition brings on record written instructions vide No.B/1761/2017 dated 05.07.2023 and the relevant portion of the said written instructions reads as under:
"The applications submitted by the writ petitioners dated 05.01.2023 and 02.02.2023 are not considered because they have not adduced any material evidence in support of their claim for the enhancement of land compensation @Rs.20,00,000/- to Rs.25,00,000/- to refer the cases to the Presiding Officer U/s 64 of LA R&R Authority for the Telangana State, Hyderabad for consideration".
4. The relevant portion of Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land K. Narasimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182284382/
1 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 reads as under:
(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:

sentences.text:
Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority:
Provided further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be,
requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days.

(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made-- (a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 21, or within six months from the date of the Collectors award,
whichever period shall first expire:
Provided further that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the said period, within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified in the first proviso."
5. A bare perusal of Section 64 clause (1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 clearly indicates that any person interested, who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the WP_17532_2023 SN,J matter may be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be, whether his objection be to the measurement of land, the amount of compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of rehabilitation and resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

opennyai_summary.decision:
It is represented by learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition that the writ petition could be disposed of directing respondent Nos.2 and 3 to consider the petitioners applications dated 05.01.2023 and 02.02.2023 filed by the petitioners seeking reference of the Award No.12/2019,
dated 24.07.2019 and Award No.13/2019, dated 30.07.2019 to the competent Authority for re-determination of compensation in respect of the land in Sy.No.265, WP_17532_2023 SN,J admeasuring Ac.41-12 guntas situated at Pothireddypally Village, Thimmajipet Mandal,
Nagarkurnool District as per Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013.
7. Taking into consideration the above said submission and duly considering Section 64 Clause (1) of the Act, 2013, the writ petition is disposed of directing respondent Nos.2 and 3 to consider and refer the petitioners' applications, dated 05.01.2023 and 02.02.2023 filed by the petitioners with a request to refer the Award No.12/2019, dated 24.07.2019 and Award No.13/2019, dated 30.07.2019 to the competent Authority for re-determination of compensation in respect of the land in Sy.No.265, admeasuring Ac.41-12 guntas situated at Pothireddypally Village, Thimmajipet Mandal,
Nagarkurnool District, within a period of two (02) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.
